title: Finite filtered page functor with normalized successor maps
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], and let $U$ range over integer-indexed cochain complexes of $\mathcal C$ with finite decreasing filtrations by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration]. Suppose maps $\varphi(U,p,r):F^pU/F^{p+r}U\to F^{p-r+1}U/F^{p+1}U$, $r\ge1$, satisfy the source-projection equation of [lem-sp-bounded-filtered-page-core]. Then the functor $S$ to cohomological spectral sequences starting at page one [def-sp-spectral-sequence] and the comparison data asserted by [lem-sp-bounded-filtered-page-core] can be chosen so that, in addition, the following holds. Identify each page $S(U)_r^{p,q}$ with $Q_r^{p,q}(U)=Z_r^{p,p+q}/B_r^{p,p+q}$ [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] as in that statement. For every $r\ge1$ and every bidegree $(p,q)$, the successor isomorphism $e_{U,r}^{p,q}:H(S(U)_r)^{p,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}S(U)_{r+1}^{p,q}$ is the unique isomorphism normalized as in [lem-sp-filtered-complex-normalized-homology] for the page differential of $S(U)_r$: for $z\in Z_{r+1}^{p,p+q}\subseteq Z_r^{p,p+q}$ the class of $z$ in $Q_r^{p,q}(U)$ is a $d_r$-cycle, and $e_{U,r}^{p,q}$ sends its homology class to the class of $z$ in $Q_{r+1}^{p,q}(U)$. For every filtered map $f:U\to V$ these isomorphisms are the successor maps of the morphism $S(f)$: $S(f)_{r+1}\circ e_{U,r}^{p,q}=e_{V,r}^{p,q}\circ H(S(f)_r)^{p,q}$. No bound on cochain degrees is imposed.

proof.text: Construct the boundary containments using [lem-sp-filtered-complex-boundaries-le-cycles]. Retain the normalized representative equations when carrying out the proof of [lem-sp-filtered-quotient-comparisons]: the private helper normalizedPage_comparisons in the item repeats that proof with the general-page representative equation kept in the conclusion. It uses the already proved representative comparison, first-page comparison and naturality helpers of that module. Choose the uniquely specified representative differentials using [lem-sp-filtered-complex-page-differential]. No cochain-degree bound is used.

proof.text: For this fixed family $D(U,r)$ take the canonical chain maps $m(t,r)$ of [lem-sp-filtered-quotient-page-maps]. They have the four-square characterization for filtration restrictions, graded descent, cycle restriction and boundary quotient descent. The same statement gives $m(1_U,r)=1$ and $m(t t\prime,r)=m(t,r)m(t\prime,r)$. Thus the maps on all positive pages have their required category laws before any successor maps are chosen.

For every $U,r,a=(p,q)$ choose the unique isomorphism $e(U,r,a):H(D(U,r).\mathrm{page})^a\cong Q_{r+1}^a(U)$ from [lem-sp-filtered-complex-normalized-homology]. To interpret its normalization without elements of an abstract abelian category, use [lem-sp-filtered-complex-successor-cycles-cover]: there is an epic $f:Z_{r+1}^{p,p+q}\to\operatorname{cycles}(D(U,r).\mathrm{page})^a$ with $f\iota=\operatorname{ofLE}(Z_{r+1}\le Z_r)\pi_r$. In particular the successor-cycle classes are cycles, and the normalization is exactly $f\pi_H e(U,r,a)=\pi_{r+1}$. This proves the asserted representative rule, including uniqueness, for the chosen differential.

source.place: Tags 012K/012M: section-filtered-complex, quotient-of-cycles description of the successor page

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-filtered-quotient-homology-naturality] to $D$, $m$ and the normalized $e$ just chosen. It gives $H(m(t,r))^a e(V,r,a)=e(U,r,a)m(t,r+1)^a$. Define $S(U)$ to have page $D(U,r).\mathrm{page}$ and successor isomorphism $e(U,r,a)$, and define $S(t)_r=m(t,r)$. The displayed equation is precisely the morphism compatibility in [def-sp-spectral-sequence]; the pagewise identity and composition laws in [lem-sp-filtered-quotient-page-maps] give the functor laws. Take $e_Z:S(U)_r^{p,q}\cong Q_r^{p,q}(U)$ to be the identity. Thus the normalized isomorphisms are the actual successor maps of this single functor, and the equation in the question holds.

The helper normalizedPage_comparisons retains, for each U,p,q,r, the representative-normalized quotient-image comparison from [lem-sp-filtered-complex-quotient-image-comparison], identifying its transition with the supplied phi by cancellation of the epic source projection. Its maps z and g satisfy z pi eQ iota = g piH H(phi). The proof of the existing comparison_on_representatives helper identifies z with the epic map of [lem-sp-filtered-complex-representative-epis] by its monic inclusion square. Since our page objects are the actual cokernels, take eI=eQ and eZ to be identity. The retained equation is exactly the asserted representative equation.

source.place: Tag 012K: section-filtered-complex, cycle/boundary quotients and quotient-complex image description

proof.text:
Fix a filtered $t:U\to V$ and put $n=p+q$. Use the step, quotient and graded maps $s,a,b,g_{\rm gr}$ of [lem-sp-filtered-quotient-comparisons], and the representative restriction $\rho:R_r(U)\to R_r(V)$ of [lem-sp-filtered-quotient-map-restrictions]. Take $k_Z,k$ satisfying the cycle and quotient squares. By [lem-sp-filtered-quotient-page-maps], $k=m(t,r)^{p,q}$. Cancel the source quotient projection to get $a\varphi_V=\varphi_U b$. Cancel the respective monic inclusions to get $\rho z_V=z_Uk_Z$ and $\rho g_V=g_U Z^n(a)$. Consequently the normalization from [lem-sp-filtered-complex-quotient-image-comparison] and the defining projection equations of the induced cohomology maps give
$$z_U\pi_U k e_I^V\iota_V=\rho g_V\pi_H H^n(\varphi_V)=g_U\pi_H H^n(a)H^n(\varphi_V)=z_U\pi_U e_I^U\iota_U H^n(b).$$
Cancel the epic $z_U\pi_U$ from Step 5. This proves the required image-comparison naturality for the same page maps and normalized $e_I$.

Set $e_1=e_H$ on our first page. At $r=1$ the source quotient complex of $\varphi$ is $\operatorname{gr}^pU$. The representative projections and cycle lifts in [lem-sp-filtered-quotient-comparisons] and [lem-sp-filtered-complex-quotient-image-comparison] coincide, since their composites with the corresponding monic inclusions are the same. Their normalization equations therefore give
$$z\pi_1 e_I(1)\iota=g\pi_H H(\varphi)=z\pi_1 e_1 H(\varphi).$$
Cancel the epic $z\pi_1$ to obtain the required first-page image equation. For a filtered map, [lem-sp-filtered-quotient-comparisons] supplies $k_1e_H^V=e_H^UH(g_{\rm gr})$ for every quotient descent $k_1$ for this same graded map. The four-square property in [lem-sp-filtered-quotient-page-maps] identifies $k_1$ with $S(t)_1$. This proves first-page naturality.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-filtered-quotient-canonical-structure] to this $S(U)$, the normalized family $e_H$, and $e_Z=1$. Its differential hypothesis holds because our page differential is $D(U,r)$ by construction. The lemma supplies the first differential as the connecting homomorphism with both specified quotient-projection equations. It also supplies the type-zero exact couple $X$, $e_D$ and $e_C$ with all the filtration-inclusion, initial-gamma and derived-differential equations required by the page-core statement. Its hypotheses involve only the pages, their differentials and $e_H$, so our choice of the normalized successor maps satisfies every hypothesis.

proof.text: For this very same $S,e_1,U,X,e_D,e_C$, apply [lem-sp-bounded-filtered-couple-abutment]. Its hypotheses on alpha and initial gamma are exactly the equations obtained in Step 8. It supplies $G^pH^n(U)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(F^pU)\to H^n(U))$, finiteness and separatedness, the limit subobjects $L$, alpha-colimits $A$, their isomorphisms $a_H$ and the specified cocone equation, convergence of $X$ and the infinite-page comparison with $\operatorname{gr}^pG H^{p+q}(U)$. Thus these are witnesses for our normalized functor, not for an independently chosen functor.

proof.text: Reuse the proved private stabilization helpers of [lem-sp-bounded-filtered-page-core] for this same S, with its identity quotient comparisons. The helper pageCore_subobjects_stabilize uses finite filtration bounds a,b to stabilize the cycle and boundary formulas. The helper pageCore_differentials_stabilize identifies the incoming source and outgoing target as zero outside the finite filtration support. Take the maximum of their two positive thresholds. At any later page, compare its stabilized cycle and boundary subobjects with those at the common threshold; pageCore_quotient_iso gives the isomorphism between the actual cokernel page objects. This uses only [def-sp-filtration] and the formulas of [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients], and works for cochain complexes unbounded in both directions.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q93-47a5e2dc3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all 15 cited statements in full, plus the Lean records of page-core and quotient-comparisons. The statement, stmt_deps and blueprint fields are unchanged from the side-project base, so the statement is not weakened. Steps 1-4 build the functor from the unique differentials D, the four-square page maps m and the normalized successor isomorphisms e. The successor-cycles-cover lemma shows the normalization is not vacuous, and homology-naturality gives exactly Mathlib's SpectralSequence.Hom.comm (Basic.lean 37-61). Steps 5-10 rebuild every page-core clause for this same functor. Step 5: the image comparison's z is epic because representative-epis gives an epi with the same domain (complexCycleRepresentatives) and the same composite with a monic. Step 6: I redid the diagram chase (a phi_V = phi_U b, rho z_V = z_U k_Z, rho g_V = g_U Z(a), then cancel the epi z_U pi_U); it gives page-core's image-naturality clause exactly. Step 7: at r=1 the representatives coincide, and the 'every k_1' clause of quotient-comparisons plus the four-square property give first-page naturality with the same s and g. Steps 8-9: the hypotheses of canonical-structure (eZ=1, d_E eZ = eZ D) and of couple-abutment (alpha and initial gamma) are met, and their conclusions match page-core's exact-couple, convergence and abutment block clause by clause. Step 10: with R=max(1,b-p,p+1-a), Z_r and B_r are constant (Stacks 012K formulas, 012W proof) and both differentials land in or come from zero graded pieces. Sources checked: Stacks homology.tex 012K (l.5955), 012M, 012N, 012O, 012P and 012W (l.6362), with tag labels verified; blueprint main-20261015 lem-kun-0f0f proof. Edge cases tested: zero complex, one-column filtration, zero differential, r=1, negative indices, and complexes unbounded in degree. No new nodes. The item duplicates none of canonical-functor, page-realization, page-construction, canonical-sequence (page 2 only) or positive-pages. No SGA. I accept all 11 declared lem-sp-* tool_uses as generic filtered-complex tools: the Künneth unit cites no units, and the parent node already uses page-core as a tool. No changes.
